title: weakness-registry-v2 lane threat list
description: One file per language lane: code/specs/data/weakness-registry-v2/lanes/<lang>.json. See VER15a section 6. The schema checks shape only. Several mandatory rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are the validator's job (VER15a section 9): every id in exclude_requires, discharge_requires and registry_evidence_map must appear in the same threat's closed_by; floor_label must be at least the registry floor; the safe_subset must belong to the registry class (or the lane-extension table); a row's stored status must equal the status recomputed from the evidence states.

lane.description: Must equal the file name without .json.

family.description: Language family, which decides which evidence kinds may close which classes (VER15a section 5).

sources.description: Where the lane-specific classes came from (a MITRE view, the language specification, a prior CVE study).

toolchain.description: The compilers or interpreters the evidence is produced with, so a claim names what it ran under.

considered_not_included.description: Weakness classes from the named sources that were considered and left out, each with the reason.

packages.description: Per-package status of every threat. Keys are package names within the lane (for example logic-gates).

label.description: Proof labels, weakest to strongest (VER31 section 4). none means no evidence of that row exists. A registry floor bounded(k) maps to the label bounded with the k recorded in the row's bound_k.

floor.description: A label a discharge must reach. none is not a floor.

kind.description: source-ref: a claim backed only by a file:line or documentation passage in the package (VER15a section 5.2). Never live; never in a route list.

id.description: Stable id the validator resolves, such as analyzer-rule:c.no-pointer-array-heap.

state.description: live: a named, MERGED repository tool establishes it at report time (the tool field names it). claimed: the evidence exists but no repository tool checks it at report time. planned: named work item, not yet built. unverified: an attestation about the language, which nothing checks.

tool.description: The merged tool that establishes the item at report time. Required when state is live.

ref.description: Where the evidence can be opened. Required for a live proof item.

planned_item.description: Backlog id; required when state is planned. Matched exactly against the backlog (VER15a section 9 rule 13); the widened pattern lets LGE-R-python be written as the backlog writes it. A template row such as LGE-L-<lane> is matched by LGE-L-<any lane id>.

origin.description: registry-v2: one of the 29 registry classes (cwe required). lane: a class the language adds.

applicability.description: A reviewer's claim, not a closure. not-applicable never closes a row by itself: only a signed-off language_exclusion on the VER15a section 5.5 whitelist does.

exclude_requires.description: Closure ids that must ALL be live for status excluded.

discharge_requires.description: Closure ids that must ALL be live, with evidence reaching floor_label, for status discharged.

language_exclusion.description: Proposes the distinct status excluded-by-language. Valid only for a (lane, CWE) pair on the VER15a section 5.5 whitelist, and only counts when signed_off is true.

requires_closed.description: Threat ids of the same file that must themselves be closed (excluded or discharged) before this threat's exclusion counts. Used for the C memory extension: memory-addressing exclusions hold only for a UB-free package.

cannot_close_in_package.description: The class cannot be closed from inside the package (for example the caller narrows the value before the call). The row stays open and every release says so.

safe_subset.description: The registry safe_subsets entry (or a VER15a section 5.5 lane extension, written lane-extension:<name>) that the exclusion route corresponds to. Required for a registry-v2 threat with exclude_requires.

registry_floor.description: Echo of the registry class's minimum_proof_label (proved, bounded(k), proved-to-gate-level); the validator compares it to the registry.

floor_label.description: The label a discharge must reach. For a registry-v2 threat it must be at least the registry floor (bounded(k) maps to bounded); a lane threat chooses its own.

registry_evidence_map.description: For a registry-v2 threat with a discharge route: every required_evidence id of the registry class mapped to the closure ids (all inside discharge_requires) that supply it.

status.description: excluded: machine-checked. excluded-by-language: whitelisted language semantics, signed off, never counted as excluded. discharged: machine-checked evidence at or above the floor. open: everything else, including every row whose closing evidence is claimed.

reached.description: The strongest label the row's evidence supports as claimed. It is a statement of the evidence, not of the status.

bound_k.description: Required when reached is bounded: the k of the registry's bounded(k).

reason.description: Why the row has this status. For an open row it is rendered after the word 'open:' in a release, and starts with 'Evidence claimed, not machine-checked' when any closing item is claimed.

ref.description: file:line, a BUILD line, a PR number or a spec section: something a reader can open. Never a backlog row.

becomes_when.description: Closure ids (kind:slug, resolved against the threat's closed_by) or hyphenated backlog ids (such as LGE-W1). Never free text (VER15a section 5.1).

no_planned_closure.description: An open row with no planned work that closes it.

reviewed_at_commit.description: A commit hash, or pr-<n> while the package is not yet on main.
